subject: worldnews
title: Syrian man charged by Danish police over alleged terror attempt
text: COPENHAGEN (Reuters) - Danish police have charged a 30-year-old Syrian man, who is an asylum seeker in Sweden, with attempting a terrorist act in Copenhagen in November 2016, a police statement said. Media are barred from naming the man, who was arrested on Thursday in an operation involving Denmark's intelligence service, police said. The court found reasonable grounds to suspect that he had planned a terror attack at an unspecified location in Copenhagen in November 2016, together with a man convicted in Germany in July of plotting an attack in Copenhagen. According to police, the two intended to kill or injure several random people by attacking them with knives and then to set off one or more explosive devices.

subject: politicsNews
title: Paul Ryan to rule out 2016 presidential run, House Speaker's aide says
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - U.S. House Speaker Paul Ryan will address the media on Tuesday to rule himself out as a 2016 presidential candidate, one of his aides said. “He’s going to rule himself out and put this to rest once and for all,” the aide said. Ryan is due to speak at Republican National Committee headquarters at 3:15 pm EST (1915 GMT). Earlier on Tuesday, in a radio interview in Wisconsin, Ryan said he wanted to be “crystal clear” that he would not allow his name to be put forward for the presidential nomination at the party's July convention.

subject: politicsNews
title: Exclusive: McCain says no one should 'leap to conclusions' that Trump will drop 'one China' policy
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Senator John McCain said on Monday that he personally supports Washington’s decades-old “one China” policy and urged people not to “leap to conclusions” that President-elect Donald Trump will abandon it. “I do not respond to every comment by the president-elect because it may be reversed the next day,” McCain told Reuters when asked about Trump’s weekend remark that the United States was not necessarily bound to its position that Taiwan is part of “one China.” McCain added, however, that “somebody should hold China responsible” for its conduct on Taiwan, Hong Kong, island building in the South China Sea and “propping up” North Korea. Trump's comments, along with his recent phone call with Taiwan's president, have provoked an angry reaction from Beijing.

subject: politicsNews
title: White House: Trump and Erdogan discuss Qatar-Gulf dispute
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump spoke with Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan on Friday about the rift between Qatar and a group of Gulf and Arab powers that have cut diplomatic and travel ties with Doha. The White House said in a statement that the two leaders discussed ways to resolve the dispute “while ensuring that all countries work together to stop terrorist funding and to combat extremist ideology”. Turkey has sided with Doha in its dispute with the four Arab states, which are boycotting Qatar over alleged backing for terrorism in what has become the worst Gulf Arab crisis in years. Doha denies the accusations.

subject: worldnews
title: Merkel ally says German parties must strike coalition deal this weekend
text: BERLIN (Reuters) - Angela Merkel's conservatives are prepared to make further concessions on cutting coal emissions in order to rescue talks with two smaller parties on forming a government, an ally of the German chancellor said on Thursday. Volker Kauder, parliamentary leader of Merkel's conservatives, said the conservatives, the Greens and the pro-business Free Democrats (FDP) could still reach a deal this weekend despite deep differences over climate and migration. “Despite the big stumbling blocks I believe it could work,” Kauder told reporters. “I feel readiness on all sides and everyone has to make concessions. And I believe that the exploratory talks must end this weekend.”

subject: politicsNews
title: Senate Democratic leader presses Trump to label China a currency manipulator
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Senator Chuck Schumer, the top Democrat in the U.S. Senate, called on Republican President Donald Trump on Tuesday to follow through on a campaign pledge and declare China a currency manipulator. “Mr. President: if you really want to put America first, label China a currency manipulator,” Schumer told reporters. According to a Senate Finance Committee document seen by Reuters on Monday, Trump’s Treasury secretary nominee, Steven Mnuchin, told senators he would work to fight currency manipulation but did not clearly say whether he currently believes China is manipulating its yuan.

subject: politicsNews
title: Priebus says 'salacious garbage' in Russia report 'didn't happen': NBC
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - President-elect Donald Trump and his incoming chief of staff pushed back on Wednesday against reports that Russian officials had put together a file of compromising information about the Republican businessman, nine days before he is due to enter the White House. Trump spokesman Reince Priebus, asked about the report on NBC’s “Today” show, said he had raised it with Trump. “He said it was ‘total garbage and I’m keeping it clean,’” Priebus said. On Twitter, Trump cited the Kremlin’s denial of the report, calling it a “complete and total fabrication.”

subject: politicsNews
title: Merkel and Hollande want Assad held to account for 'criminal acts'
text: BERLIN (Reuters) - German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Francois Hollande discussed the situation in Syria on Friday and want to keep working to hold Syrian President Bashar al-Assad accountable for “criminal acts”, according to a statement from Berlin. Earlier on Friday the United States fired dozens of cruise missiles at a Syrian air base from which it said a chemical weapons attack was launched this week. “President Assad alone is responsible for this development,” the German government said in a statement issued after the two leaders spoke by phone on Friday morning. It said Assad's repeated use of chemical weapons and his crimes against the Syrian people should lead to sanctions. “Germany and France call on the international community.... to campaign together for a political transition in Syria,” the statement said.

subject: worldnews
title: Britain's Johnson tries to clarify comments on jailed aid worker in Iran
text: LONDON (Reuters) - British Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson said on Tuesday that his comments last week about a jailed Iranian-British aid worker could have been clearer, adding that he had not meant to lend credibility to Iranian accusations against her. On Nov. 1, Johnson said Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe had been training people in journalism before her arrest in Iran in April 2016. “The UK government has no doubt that she was on holiday in Iran when she was arrested last year and that was the sole purpose of her visit,” Johnson said. “My point was that I disagreed with the Iranian view that training journalists was a crime, not that I wanted to lend any credence to Iranian allegations that Mrs Zaghari-Ratcliffe had been engaged in such activity,” he said. “I accept that my remarks could have been clearer in that respect and I am glad to provide this clarification.” Johnson said he would visit Iran in the coming weeks to discuss all consular matters.

subject: worldnews
title: Irish PM says Britain will put forward new wording on Irish border
text: DUBLIN (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Theresa May told Irish Prime Minister Leo Varadkar that she would offer suggestions to Brexit negotiators within the next 24 hours in an effort to end the deadlock over the Irish border, Varadkar said on Wednesday. “We discussed the idea certainly but we didn’t discuss any particular words or combination of words or language but I certainly indicated a willingness to consider any proposals that the UK side have,” Varadkar told a news conference after a phone call with May earlier on Wednesday. “Having consulted with people in London, she wants to come back to us with some text tonight or tomorrow. I expressed my willingness to consider that because I want us to move to phase two if that is possible next week.”

subject: worldnews
title: May to meet Bill Clinton to talk about Northern Ireland crisis
text: LONDON (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Theresa May will meet former U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday morning to talk about the political crisis in Northern Ireland, her spokesman said. As president, Clinton played a central part in brokering peace in the British province, where a power-sharing government collapsed in January and the opposing sides have been unable to end the stalemate since. Clinton travelled to Belfast this week to meet the political parties and try to help break the deadlock. “He and the PM wanted to take this opportunity to discuss Northern Ireland ..,” May's spokesman said. “Obviously work is ongoing in trying to reach a solution and to get the compromises that are necessary to get the devolved administration up and running again,” he added. Earlier, the British government minister for the province said the prospects of a deal there were “not positive”. The meeting with Clinton is scheduled for 0830 GMT in May's Downing Street office.

subject: politicsNews
title: Obama says he doesn't believe FBI's Comey is trying to sway the election
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - President Barack Obama said on Friday that he does not think FBI Director James Comey was trying to influence the presidential election when he decided that the agency would review newly discovered emails in its investigation of Hillary Clinton’s private email server. “Now I’ve said before and I’ll say again, Jim Comey is a good man,” Obama said in an MSNBC interview. “And I do not believe that he is in any way trying to influence the election one way or another. I think he is a serious public servant who wants to do the right thing,” Obama said.

subject: worldnews
title: Five migrants injured by gunfire during brawl in Calais
text: LILLE, France (Reuters) - Five migrants were injured on Saturday when shots were fired during a fight in the northern French port of Calais, the local prefect's office said. It said groups of Afghans exchanged gunfire in the late afternoon. A police source said the incident was “probably a dispute between migrant smugglers.” The shots were fired close to the Secours Catholique charity on the outskirts of Calais. Three of the migrants were being treated at a hospital in Calais, a fourth who was more seriously hurt had been moved to a hospital in Lille, and a fifth was treated at the scene. Calais attracts migrants hoping to reach Britain, which lies a short distance across the Channel. Authorities cleared the makeshift “Jungle” camp in Calais last year, but people hoping to cross to Britain by train or ferry have been steadily coming back. Authorities estimate that 500 migrants from Ethiopia, Eritrea and Afghanistan remain in Calais, while charities put the figure at 700.

subject: worldnews
title: UK's May does not mention possibility of leaving EU before March 2019
text: LONDON (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Theresa May did not raise the possibility of leaving the European Union before March 2019 in her speech in Florence on Friday, despite a report in the Telegraph newspaper that she would. Minutes before the speech began, the Telegraph reported that May would put forward the option of departing the bloc ahead of Britain's scheduled exit at the end of March 2019, which sent sterling down about 30 ticks. Responding to a question after the speech, May said Britain would leave at the end of March 2019. (This story corrects to add a dropped word in the lede)

subject: politicsNews
title: Mulvaney: government shutdown may be unavoidable if Democrats don't improve
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - White House budget director Mick Mulvaney on Tuesday accused Democrats of trying to make President Donald Trump look bad by claiming victory in the budget talks, and said a government shutdown might be unavoidable if they do not behave better. Asked about Trump’s tweet on a possible shutdown in September, Mulvaney said: “I think the president is frustrated with the fact that he negotiated in good faith with the Democrats and they went out to try to spike the football and make him look bad.” “We’ve got a lot to do between now and September. I don’t anticipate a shutdown in September, but if the Democrats aren’t going to behave any better than they have in the last couple of days, it may be inevitable,” he said.

subject: politicsNews
title: Clinton to return to campaign trail Thursday, 'details to come'
text: WHITE PLAINS, N.Y. (Reuters) - Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton, who is recovering from pneumonia, plans to restart campaigning on Thursday, her spokesman said. Spokesman Nick Merrill said on Tuesday that Clinton “has spent the day catching up on reading briefings, making calls” and watching on television as President Barack Obama spoke at a campaign event for the former secretary of state in Philadelphia. “We will resume campaign travel on Thursday, more details to come,” he added. Hours after Clinton, 68, nearly collapsed on Sunday at a New York memorial ceremony for the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks, her doctor said she had been diagnosed with pneumonia two days earlier. Clinton said on Monday that she would rest for a few days before returning to her campaign for the Nov. 8 election against Republican Donald Trump. She said she had ignored her doctor’s advice to rest and had not disclosed her diagnosis earlier because “I just didn’t think it was going to be that big a deal.”

subject: worldnews
title: Saudi King Salman tells Putin Iran must stop meddling in Middle East: Interfax
text: MOSCOW (Reuters) - Iran must stop interfering in the Middle East, visiting Saudi King Salman told Russian President Vladimir Putin during their Kremlin meeting on Thursday, Russia's Interfax news agency reported. “We emphasize that the security and stability of the Gulf region and the Middle East is an urgent necessity for achieving stability and security in Yemen,” Salman was quoted as saying by the agency. “This would demand that Iran give up interference with the internal affairs of the region, to give up actions destabilizing the situation in this region.”

subject: worldnews
title: White House: U.S. will talk to North Korea only about freeing detained Americans
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The Trump administration will hold no talks with North Korea at this time apart from possible discussions about freeing U.S. citizens detained there, the White House said on Monday. “We’ve been clear that now is not the time to talk,” White House spokeswoman Sarah Sanders told reporters, expanding on a weekend tweet from President Donald Trump that had been seen as undercutting Secretary of State Rex Tillerson. “The only conversations that have taken place, or that would, would be on bringing back Americans who have been detained,” Sanders said. “Beyond that, there will be no conversations with North Korea at this time.”

subject: worldnews
title: Peru's Kuczynski loses support of key ministers amid scandal: sources
text: LIMA (Reuters) - Peruvian President Pedro Pablo Kuczynski has lost the backing of senior cabinet members after it emerged that he had business ties to Brazilian company Odebrecht, which is embroiled in scandal, two government sources said on Thursday, as opposition figures called for him to quit. The sources said cabinet members were stunned on Wednesday to learn of payments that Odebrecht said it had made to a company controlled by Kuczynski, who had repeatedly denied any links to the construction firm. Key ministers and lawmakers in Kuczynski's party want him to resign, the sources said, speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the matter. Kuczynski has denied earning anything improperly and offered to explain the matter to Congress.

subject: worldnews
title: U.S. official: U.N. envoy carries no U.S. government message on North Korea trip
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - U.N. envoy Jeffrey Feltman, a former senior U.S. State Department official, is not delivering any message from the U.S. government during his visit to North Korea for talks on behalf of the United Nations, the State Department said on Tuesday. Feltman is currently the U.N. undersecretary-general for political affairs; he previously served as U.S. assistant secretary of state for Near Eastern affairs. “We’re certainly aware of his travels under the auspices of his role with the United Nations to North Korea,” State Department spokeswoman Heather Nauert told reporters. “He’s not traveling on behalf of the U.S. government and he’s not traveling - I want to make this clear - with any kind of message from the U.S. government.”

subject: politicsNews
title: German defense minister expects U.S. to honor longstanding commitment to Europe
text: BERLIN (Reuters) - Germany should act as a “bridge-builder” to U.S. President-elect Donald Trump and help answer open questions about his views on conflicts in Iraq and Syria and on U.S. ties with Europe, Defence Minister Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday. Asked by Reuters whether she worried that the United States under Trump might reduce its support for Europe or Germany at a time of heightened threat from Russia, von der Leyen said she expected Washington to keep to its longstanding commitment to trans-Atlantic ties. “Our expectation is that the American commitment to that friendship will continue unabated,” she said. “My wish is that we find a common basis for understanding because the problems ... are big enough and we must tackle them together.”

subject: worldnews
title: May to speak with Trump about Jerusalem, says its status must be settled through negotiation
text: LONDON (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Theresa May said she plans to talk to U.S. President Donald Trump about the status of Jerusalem, which she said should be decided as part of a settlement between Israel and the Palestinians. She said the ancient city should eventually be shared between Israel and a future Palestinian state, and that there should be a sovereign and viable Palestinian state as part of a two-state solution. “I’m intending to speak to President Trump about this matter,” May said. “The status of Jerusalem should be determined in a negotiated settlement between the Israelis and the Palestinians.” “Jerusalem should ultimately form a shared capital between the Israeli and Palestinian states,” May said.

subject: politicsNews
title: House committee delays Puerto Rico hearing
text: NEW YORK (Reuters) - The U.S. House of Representatives Committee on Natural Resources, which has oversight of Puerto Rico, on Thursday postponed indefinitely a hearing on the island’s recovery from Hurricane Maria and the role of a federally appointed oversight board. A committee spokesman said the hearing, which had been scheduled for Oct. 24, would be rescheduled because of scheduling conflicts among witnesses. Earlier on Thursday, President Donald Trump said he would work with Congress to approve grants and loans to help rebuild Puerto Rico after last month’s devastating hurricane.

subject: worldnews
title: EU's Barnier warns that no Brexit deal would be 'a very bad deal'
text: BERLIN (Reuters) - EU chief Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier said on Wednesday that the bloc had to be united, and was united, in handling Britain's withdrawal, and cautioned that a failure to reach an agreement would be very damaging. “No deal would be a very bad deal,” Barnier said, switching from French to English during a speech to Germany's BDA employers' association. It was his third speech to a German audience on Brexit that day. Barnier also said he hoped that by next week progress would have been made on the principles of Britain's divorce from the EU, and that London knew it could not have one foot in the single market and one foot out of it.

subject: politicsNews
title: Trump ally Christie calls criticism of slain soldier's family 'inappropriate'
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Chris Christie, a close ally of Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump, distanced himself on Tuesday from Trump’s dispute with the Muslim family of a slain U.S. Army captain, Politico reported. Christie, the governor of New Jersey, said that criticism of the family of Captain Humayan Khan, who died in Iraq in 2004, was “inappropriate.” “I didn’t see Mr. Khan’s speech at the DNC, but I’ll just say this: I’m a father and I just cannot imagine the pain of losing a child under any circumstances,” said Christie, who backed Trump after ending his own White House bid, according to Politico, which quoted his remarks from a news conference at the New Jersey State House in Trenton.

The payments would most likely come from an obscure Treasury Department fund meant to cover federal legal claims, those executives and lawyers said. title: TRUMP TELLS State Department to cut more than 50% of funding to U.N.
text: President Trump's administration has instructed the State Department to cut more than 50 percent of U.S. funding for United Nations programs, Foreign Policy reported. The push for sharp reductions comes as the White House prepares to release its 2018 topline budget proposal on Thursday, which is expected to include a 37 percent cut to the budgets of the State Department and U.S. Agency for International Development. It is unclear whether the budget plan from the Office of Management and Budget would reflect the full scale of Trump's proposed U.N. cuts. Richard Gowan, a U.N. expert at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told FP the changes would cause “chaos” if true. “[It would] leave a gaping hole that other big donors would struggle to fill,” he said, noting that the U.S. gave $1.5 billion of the U.N. refugee agency's $4 billion budget last year. subject: worldnews
title: Poland's new government led by Morawiecki wins confidence vote
text: WARSAW (Reuters) - Poland's new government, headed by Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki, won a vote of confidence in parliament shortly before midnight on Tuesday, according to voting records, clearing the way for the Cabinet to begin work. Morawiecki, 49, was appointed prime minister last week in a reshuffle that replaced Beata Szydlo, as the ruling Law and Justice party prepares for elections over the next three years. He said Warsaw's economic policy, built on generous public spending and a growing emphasis on developing domestic capital, would stay largely unchanged, but that his government would work to improve Poland's foreign relations.

subject: politicsNews
title: Cohn: Trump tax cuts won't be made retroactive, Fox Business Network reports
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The Republican tax plan will not include retroactive adjustments, White House economic adviser Gary Cohn said on Friday, even though some U.S. lawmakers want the cuts to apply to 2017 as the party tries to pass the bill by the end of the year. “We're trying to deliver great tax reform to the American public. We can't get it retroactive to this year. We're trying to do a tax plan that starts on Jan. 1 of next year,” Cohn said in an interview with Fox Business Network. (This version of the story was refiled to correct the headline to read “Fox Business Network” rather than “Fox Business News”)

subject: worldnews
title: Kremlin warns of 'extremely negative' fallout if U.S. exits Iran nuclear deal
text: MOSCOW (Reuters) - The Kremlin said on Friday that a U.S. withdrawal from the Iran nuclear deal would have extremely negative consequences and that Iran would probably leave the agreement as well. “Certainly, this will damage the atmosphere of predictability, security, stability and non-proliferation in the entire world,” President Vladimir Putin's spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a conference call. He added that Russia would continue its policy of working to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons.

subject: politicsNews
title: Etihad and Qatar Airways to allow barred passengers back onto U.S. flights
text: DUBAI (Reuters) - Gulf carriers Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways said on Saturday that they will let passengers barred by President Donald Trump's executive order board U.S.-bound flights, after a federal judge blocked the order. U.S. Customs & Border Protection (CBP) has told both airlines they may board travelers from the seven Muslim-majority countries and all refugees who had been banned under the order, the airlines said. “Acceptance will naturally be subject to checks completed by U.S. authorities as existed prior to the issuance of the Executive Order on 27 January,” an Etihad spokesman said in emailed comments to Reuters. A Qatar Airways spokeswoman confirmed that the airline was again accepting all passengers with valid travel documents. Trump's suspension of entry for nationals of Iran, Iraq, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, along with all refugees, caught airlines off guard, and some carriers had to re-roster flight crews to comply.

subject: worldnews
title: Five Ukrainian soldiers killed in east of country, military says
text: KIEV (Reuters) - Five Ukrainian servicemen died on Thursday when pro-Russian rebels attacked government positions, mostly in the Luhansk region, the Ukrainian military said. A peace agreement now almost three years old has failed to end the fighting in eastern Ukraine, with each side accusing the other of breaching the ceasefire almost daily. In a statement, the military said the losses came during an eight-hour clash near the small village of Krymske, 30 km (20 miles) west of Luhansk. The situation in the region had worsened after a conflict between separatist factions that control the city.

subject: politicsNews
title: Scaramucci says White House will go after leakers and may restructure communications office
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - New White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci said on Tuesday that he would probably restructure the communications operation and fire staff if the leaks did not stop. “If the leaks continue, then I've got to let everybody go,” he told reporters aboard Air Force One after President Donald Trump's trip to Ohio. Scaramucci said there were no immediate plans to dismiss anyone else after the resignation earlier Tuesday of senior assistant press secretary Michael Short. He said he would take time to study the communications operation. “We will probably restructure,” he said. He and Trump were both adamant that the leaks had to end, Scaramucci said. “We've got a plan,” he said, without giving details.

subject: worldnews
title: London police stand down after Oxford Street incident
text: LONDON (Reuters) - London's police force said on Friday that it had stood down after an incident in the heart of the city's shopping district, to which officers initially responded as a possible terrorist incident. “Our response on #OxfordStreet has now been stood down,” the Metropolitan Police said on its official Twitter account. “Given the nature of the info received we responded as if the incident was terrorism, including the deployment of armed officers,” police added. They said they had found no evidence of the gunshots reported earlier and that there were no casualties.

subject: politicsNews
title: Washington Post-ABC poll puts Clinton ahead of Trump, 47-44 percent
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton holds a 3-point national lead over Republican Donald Trump in a Washington Post-ABC tracking poll released on Friday. The telephone survey of 1,768 adults, conducted Sunday through Wednesday, found Clinton at 47 percent and Trump at 44 percent, four days before Tuesday's presidential election. The margin of error was 2.5 percentage points. In the Post-ABC poll released on Wednesday, the two candidates were tied at 46 percent each.

subject: worldnews
title: Venezuela's Maduro delivers donation to Cuba after hurricane
text: HAVANA (Reuters) - Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro made a surprise visit to Cuba on Thursday evening to deliver a donation of goods after Hurricane Irma devastated the Caribbean island, Cuban state media reported on Friday. State television showed Cuban President Raul Castro greeting Maduro at Havana's airport. The two countries are close ideological and strategic allies against what they describe as U.S. imperialism. “This aid will contribute to making up for the damage caused by Hurricane Irma,” state radio station Radio Reloj said. The alliance dates to 2000, when Socialist Hugo Chavez took power in Venezuela, which has the world's largest oil reserves but is mired in a deep economic crisis. An oil-for-services arrangement, under which Cuba provides medical and technical services, underpins their economic ties and continues despite reduced Venezuelan oil deliveries and payments to Cuba. Millions of Venezuelans face food shortages and soaring inflation.

subject: politicsNews
title: Majority of U.S. Senate supports disaster aid package
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - A majority of the U.S. Senate voted on Tuesday to back a new round of disaster aid to help Puerto Rico and several states recover from hurricane and wildfire damage. The bill would provide $36.5 billion in emergency relief, with Puerto Rico in particular struggling to restore electricity and other basic services after devastating hurricanes. The House of Representatives passed the measure earlier this month. The Trump administration has already signaled that it will ask Congress for another round of emergency funding.

subject: worldnews
title: Japanese man kills wife and priestess sister with sword in bizarre family feud, media say
text: TOKYO (Reuters) - A Japanese man armed with a sword killed his sister, a Shinto priestess, on the grounds of a Tokyo shrine, then stabbed his wife to death before taking his own life, police and media said. Police declined to comment on a motive for Thursday's killings or on the family feud. Shigenaga Tomioka, 56, attacked Nagako Tomioka, 58, the chief priestess of the Tomioka Hachimangu shrine, as she stepped out of a car; media reports said she was his sister. His 49-year-old wife, Mariko, stabbed and wounded the car's driver with a sword, police said, before she too was killed. The Sankei newspaper reported that Shigenaga sent his sister a threatening letter in 2006 saying he would “send her to hell.” Shinto is Japan's traditional religion and shrines dot the country. The Tomioka Hachimangu shrine, founded in 1627, has close ties to sumo and was visited by the emperor and empress in 2012.

subject: politicsNews
title: Cohn: 'fair trade' means reciprocal tariffs, White House says
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The Trump administration wants to tax imports from countries that impose tariffs on U.S. goods, said Gary Cohn, director of President Donald Trump's National Economic Council. “Fair means we treat our trading partners the way they treat us,” Cohn told a conference on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank spring meetings in Washington on Thursday. “If you want to insist on having a tariff on a product, which we prefer you not, the president believes that we should treat you in a reciprocal fashion and that we should tax your product coming into the United States.”

subject: worldnews
title: U.S. welcomes Chinese, South Korean move to mend ties despite missile defense dispute
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The U.S. State Department on Tuesday welcomed a decision by China and South Korea to restore normal relations after a year-long standoff over Seoul and Washington's deployment of a missile defense system aimed at countering North Korea's nuclear program. “We ... were pleased to hear that the Republic of Korea, that our Korean friends, and also the Chinese are forging a closer relationship,” State Department spokeswoman Heather Nauert told a briefing. “We see that as providing better stability ... for a region that desperately needs it because of North Korea.” Nauert said South Korea and the United States had not changed their decision to deploy the THAAD missile defense system in South Korea as protection against Pyongyang's nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

subject: politicsNews
title: Trump accuses Mexico's Carlos Slim of trying to help Clinton win
text: GREENSBORO, N.C. (Reuters) - Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump accused Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim on Friday of trying to help Democrat Hillary Clinton win the Nov. 8 election through his ties to the New York Times. At a rally in Greensboro, North Carolina, Trump also repeated that the women who have accused him of unwanted sexual advances are making up their stories. Trump said Slim, as a major New York Times shareholder, was helping bankroll what he described as the paper's effort to help Clinton win the presidency. The Times had published a story in which two women accused Trump of groping them. “They're not journalists,” Trump said of the Times reporters. “They're corporate lobbyists for Carlos Slim and foreign corporations.”

subject: worldnews
title: U.S. calls on Congolese forces to show restraint and investigate violence
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The U.S. State Department called on the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Wednesday to protect civilians affected by violence in the east of the country and urged its security forces to avoid excessive force. Department spokeswoman Heather Nauert said Washington was “dismayed” by the deaths last week of 30 Burundian refugees and a Congolese soldier in the city of Kamanyola, adding: “The cause of the violence must be determined and perpetrators must be held accountable.”

subject: politicsNews
title: Factbox: Trump meets AT&T CEO and others
text: (Reuters) - U.S. President-elect Donald Trump held meetings in New York on Thursday as he prepared to take over the White House from President Barack Obama on Jan. 20. Here is a list of the confirmed meetings from Thursday, according to Trump's transition team: * Chairman and CEO of AT&T Inc (T.N), which plans to merge with Time Warner Inc (TWX.N) * Former U.S. ambassador to Uruguay, under consideration for a post at the U.S. Agency for International Development * Former U.S. ambassador to Tanzania, under consideration for a post at the U.S. Agency for International Development * Chief executive officer of 21.co and a partner at Andreessen Horowitz, under consideration for a post at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration * Managing director at Mithril Capital Management, under consideration for a post at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration * President of Portugal

subject: worldnews
title: Japan's Abe to hold phone talks with Trump on Wednesday, source says
text: TOKYO (Reuters) - Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe will speak by phone with U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday to offer condolences over the mass shooting in Las Vegas and to discuss North Korea's weapons programs, a Japanese government source said. Tensions on the Korean peninsula have risen since reclusive North Korea carried out its sixth and most powerful nuclear test on Sept. 3, prompting a new round of United Nations sanctions.

subject: politicsNews
title: Tillerson: nuclear weapons will not bring North Korea security
text: UNITED NATIONS (Reuters) - U.S. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson said on Thursday that pursuing nuclear weapons will not make North Korea's government secure and that China's help is essential to bringing Pyongyang's nuclear and missile programs under control. “North Korea may assume that nuclear weapons will ensure the survival of its regime. In truth, nuclear weapons are clearly only leading to greater isolation, ignominy and deprivation,” Tillerson told the U.N. Security Council. “If China truly desires to denuclearize the Korean peninsula to promote stability and to avoid conflict in that sensitive region right on its own border, now's the time to work with the rest of us ... to put the kind of pressure on North Korea that can change its strategic calculations before it's too late,” he said.

subject: worldnews
title: Magnitude 5.4 earthquake shakes southern Mexico; no damage reported
text: MEXICO CITY (Reuters) - A magnitude 5.4 earthquake hit southern Mexico on Friday, the U.S. Geological Survey said, with no immediate reports of damage. It was unclear whether the tremor was an aftershock of the powerful series of quakes last month that toppled buildings in Mexico City and killed nearly 500 people. The USGS said the epicenter was just off the coast of Oaxaca state in Mexico's southwest, at a depth of 59.5 kilometers (37 miles). An 8.1 magnitude quake struck Oaxaca on Sept. 7 near the town of Juchitan, flattening thousands of buildings in the humid market town. Mexico City emergency services chief Fausto Lugo said on local television that Friday's quake was felt only lightly in the capital and that no damage had been reported.

subject: politicsNews
title: Trump says travel ban should be 'larger, tougher and more specific'
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump pushed back on Friday against efforts to limit his administration's ban on entry to the United States by people from six Muslim-majority countries, which also restricts refugees, saying the controversial ban should be even broader. “The travel ban into the United States should be far larger, tougher and more specific-but stupidly, that would not be politically correct!” Trump said on Twitter. His post came ahead of a key Supreme Court hearing next month on the constitutionality of his executive order on the ban.

subject: worldnews
title: Madrid was reluctantly forced to act over Catalan vote, official says
text: BARCELONA (Reuters) - The Spanish government was reluctantly forced to send national police to stop a Catalan independence referendum that had descended into farce, the senior Spanish official in the northeastern region said on Sunday. Enric Millo, the Madrid government's representative in Catalonia, told a news conference that the National Police and Civil Guard officers who arrived at polling stations were there to seize voting materials, not to target people trying to vote. “We have been made to do something we didn't want to do,” he said. Responding to the Catalan government's announcement on Sunday that people could vote at any polling station they found open, Millo said: “It's all a sham, a farce. It is the first time in history that the rules of the game are changed 45 minutes before the start of voting.”

subject: politicsNews
title: Canada says it is ready to join NAFTA talks 'at any time'
text: OTTAWA (Reuters) - Canada is ready to attend talks on renewing the North American Free Trade Agreement at any time, a Canadian official said on Wednesday, responding to reports that a draft executive order to pull the United States out of the pact was under consideration. “At this moment NAFTA negotiations have not started. Canada is ready to come to the table at any time,” said Alex Lawrence, a spokesman for Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland.

subject: worldnews
title: Zimbabwe army hands over ex-finance minister to police, relative says
text: JOHANNESBURG (Reuters) - Former Zimbabwe finance minister Ignatius Chombo, who was detained by the military last week in an operation against “criminals” around ousted president Robert Mugabe, has been handed over to police, a relative said on Friday. The relative, who asked not to be named for fear for their safety, said Chombo had been badly beaten while in military custody. Police spokeswoman Charity Charamba said she had no information about Chombo.

subject: politicsNews
title: Kerry to travel to Saudi Arabia and France, State Department says
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Secretary of State John Kerry will leave Thursday for a trip to Saudi Arabia and France, the State Department said. In Hafr al-Batin, Saudi Arabia, Kerry will meet senior Saudi officials to discuss the crises in Syria and Yemen and other security matters, department spokesman Mark Toner said. On Saturday and Sunday he will be in Paris to meet counterparts from France, Britain, Germany, Italy and the European Union to discuss “a wide range of regional and global issues,” Toner told reporters at the daily briefing.

subject: worldnews
title: Australia resumes use of Chinese-made drones in non-classified operations
text: MELBOURNE (Reuters) - Australia has resumed using Chinese-built drones in non-classified situations, Defence Minister Marise Payne said on Thursday. The Australian defense forces had paused deployment of China-made drones while they reviewed cybersecurity, following the lead of the United States, Payne said on the sidelines of an event in Washington. The U.S. Army said in August that it had ordered personnel to stop using drones made by China's SZ DJI Technology Co Ltd because of “cyber vulnerabilities” in the products. “Following the decision of the U.S. Army, we reviewed our own use of those particular articles and paused our use of them for a while,” she said. “Following that review, we were comfortable with resuming their use in an unclassified situation.” The Australian newspaper reported that the Australian Defence Force had 40 DJI drones used in military exercises, though their exact role was not specified. DJI is a market leader in civilian drones and aerial imaging technology.

subject: politicsNews
title: Ryan: Trump playing a constructive role on healthcare
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - House Speaker Paul Ryan said on Thursday that President Donald Trump is playing a constructive role on new health care legislation and helping to bridge differences among congressional Republicans. “This president is getting deeply involved,” Ryan told a news briefing. “He is helping bridge gaps in our conference. He is a constructive force to help us get to a resolution so that we get consensus on how to repeal and replace Obamacare.”

subject: worldnews
title: Lebanon's cabinet to meet Tuesday for first time since political crisis began, media office says
text: BEIRUT (Reuters) - Lebanon's cabinet will meet on Tuesday for the first time since the country plunged into a political crisis a month ago, when Prime Minister Saad al-Hariri announced his resignation in a broadcast from Saudi Arabia. The cabinet's media office said the session would start at noon at the presidential palace. The meeting is expected to take up Hariri's resignation, which pulled Lebanon back into a regional contest between Riyadh and its main regional rival, Iran.

subject: politicsNews
title: Factbox: Trump to meet House Speaker Ryan and Sen. Manchin
text: (Reuters) - Donald Trump was scheduled to hold more meetings on Friday and Monday as he builds his administration ahead of taking over from Democratic President Barack Obama on Jan. 20. According to his transition team, the Republican president-elect has held more than 85 meetings so far. His team said Trump was due to meet the following people in the coming days: * U.S. House Speaker Paul Ryan, a Wisconsin Republican * The U.S. senator from West Virginia, a Democrat * A meeting originally set for Dec. 9: technology industry leaders invited to meet Trump, according to media reports citing transition officials.

subject: worldnews
title: CSU picks right-winger as candidate for Bavarian state premier
text: MUNICH (Reuters) - Lawmakers from Germany's Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of Chancellor Angela Merkel's conservatives, have nominated state finance minister Markus Soeder as their candidate for state premier in a regional election. CSU parliamentary group leader Thomas Kreuzer told reporters in Munich that the party's lawmakers had agreed unanimously to put forward Soeder, a fierce critic of Merkel's refugee policy, to run for state premier in next year's regional election. Soeder said he welcomed Bavarian state premier Horst Seehofer's decision to remain CSU party leader, saying it would help find a way out of the political deadlock in Berlin.

subject: politicsNews
title: Top House Democrat hopes for action on Puerto Rico bill next week
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - House Democratic Leader Nancy Pelosi said on Thursday that lawmakers were “working in a very cooperative way” to resolve Puerto Rico's debt crisis and hopefully would be closer to a solution by next week. “Hopefully, by the time we meet next week again we're closer to a solution,” Pelosi told reporters. Discussing talks with the chamber's Republican majority on a bill to help Puerto Rico handle its $70 billion debt, she said: “I don't see they're dragging it out. I think this is a legitimate process on the part of the Republicans.”

subject: worldnews
title: Putin says Iran and Turkey back proposed Syrian peoples' congress
text: SOCHI, Russia (Reuters) - The leaders of Iran and Turkey on Wednesday backed convening a Syrian peoples' congress as one of the first steps toward inclusive dialogue in the war-torn country, Russian President Vladimir Putin said. Speaking after meeting Iranian President Hassan Rouhani and Turkey's Tayyip Erdogan, Putin said the three leaders had instructed their diplomats and security and defense bodies to work out the congress's makeup and date. Putin said after the trilateral meeting in the southern Russian city of Sochi that Syria's leadership is committed to the peace process, constitutional reform and free elections. The three presidents also agreed to step up efforts to finish off “terrorist” groups in Syria, he said.

subject: politicsNews
title: Mexican foreign minister to travel to U.S. to meet Dreamers
text: MEXICO CITY (Reuters) - Mexican Foreign Minister Luis Videgaray will travel to the United States this week to meet local leaders and beneficiaries of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program, the ministry said on Monday. In a statement, the ministry said Videgaray will visit Sacramento and Los Angeles on Sept. 11-12, then Washington D.C. on Sept. 13. He will meet California Gov. Jerry Brown and other officials, it said.

subject: worldnews
title: Canada's Trudeau says he raised human rights and killings with Philippines' Duterte
text: MANILA (Reuters) - Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said on Tuesday that he raised human rights and extrajudicial killings in a conversation with Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, who he said was “receptive” to his comments. Human rights groups had urged leaders at an Asian summit in Manila to press Duterte over the thousands of Filipinos killed in his 16-month-old crackdown on illegal drugs. Trudeau said Canada has a reputation for speaking frankly with partners everywhere about issues such as the rule of law and human rights. “I also mentioned human rights, rule of law and specifically extra judicial killings as being an issue that Canada is concerned with,” he told a news conference in Manila. “I will always bring that up. The president was receptive to my comments and it was throughout a very cordial and positive exchange.”

subject: politicsNews
title: Trump working with GOP leaders to adjust healthcare plan, spokesman says
text: ABOARD AIR FORCE ONE (Reuters) - President Donald Trump is working with Republican leaders in the House of Representatives to change their healthcare overhaul so that it has enough support to pass, a White House spokesman said on Wednesday. “We're obviously in talks with Speaker (Paul) Ryan, the entire leadership team over there ... to get the best outcome based on feedback from members,” White House spokesman Sean Spicer told reporters at a briefing.

subject: worldnews
title: U.S. urges Northern Ireland parties to keep talking on power-sharing, State Department says
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The United States on Wednesday urged the parties in Northern Ireland to continue their dialogue toward a power-sharing agreement, after the British government moved to impose a budget on the region. “While we understand the issues under discussion between both parties are complex and sensitive, we share the UK and Irish governments' belief that these can be resolved in a spirit of shared political responsibility and pragmatism,” the State Department said in a statement. London moved on Wednesday to set Northern Ireland's budget directly after the province's main parties failed to agree on restoring a power-sharing government that collapsed in January.

subject: politicsNews
title: Merkel adviser: Germany to reach out to Trump administration to preserve good ties
text: BERLIN (Reuters) - Germany wants to reach out to the incoming U.S. administration of President-elect Donald Trump to safeguard vital trans-Atlantic relations, Chancellor Angela Merkel's foreign policy adviser Christoph Heusgen said on Wednesday. Speaking to lawmakers from Merkel's conservative party, Heusgen also said Germany would have to take on more international responsibility in the future. He said Berlin would steadily raise military spending toward the NATO target of 2 percent of gross domestic product. Earlier, Merkel said there would be contacts at all levels with the United States ahead of this year's Group of 20 meetings, which Germany chairs.

subject: worldnews
title: South Korean police seek arrest warrant for Hanjin Group chairman
text: SEOUL (Reuters) - South Korean police are seeking an arrest warrant for Cho Yang-ho, chairman of Hanjin Group, parent of Korean Air Lines Co Ltd, on breach-of-trust charges after an investigation into construction work at his home, a police official said on Monday. In July, police raided the headquarters of Korean Air Lines, the country's top airline, as part of a probe into allegations that company funds were used to pay for renovations at Cho's residence. A Korean Air spokesman declined to comment.

subject: politicsNews
title: Trump says he will submit healthcare reforms in early to mid-March
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he would submit his planned changes to the Affordable Care Act in early or mid-March. “We're doing Obamacare, we're in the final stages,” Trump told a news conference, adding: “So we will be submitting sometime in early March, mid-March.” Trump campaigned last year on a promise to repeal and replace Obamacare, the signature healthcare program of his predecessor, President Barack Obama.

subject: worldnews
title: Kremlin says Syria peoples' congress is being 'actively discussed'
text: MOSCOW (Reuters) - A proposal to convene a congress of all of Syria's ethnic groups is a joint initiative promoted by Russia and others and is now under active discussion, the Kremlin said on Friday. It is too early, though, to talk about the date and venue of the congress, which is viewed as a mechanism to support Syria's post-war development, Putin's spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a conference call. Putin raised the idea of holding such a congress at a forum with foreign scholars on Thursday.

subject: politicsNews
title: New York Republican Zeldin says he opposes tax bill
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Republican U.S. Representative Lee Zeldin said he would not support the tax reform bill introduced by Republican congressional leaders on Thursday. “I am a ‘no' to this bill in its current form. We need to fix this state and local tax deduction issue. Adding back in the property tax deduction up to $10,000 is progress, but not enough progress,” Zeldin said in a statement. Several New York lawmakers opposed eliminating the state and local tax deduction.

subject: worldnews
title: Britain 'unconditionally committed' to European security, PM May says
text: TAPA, Estonia (Reuters) - Prime Minister Theresa May said on Friday that Britain will stay “unconditionally committed” to protecting Europe after it leaves the European Union, pointing to the need to unite against threats from Russia. “When a nation like Russia deliberately violates the rules-based international order that we have worked so hard to create, we must come together with our allies to defend that international system,” she told British troops in northern Estonia. “The United Kingdom is unconditionally committed to maintaining Europe's security and we will continue to offer aid and assistance to EU member states that are the victims of armed aggression, terrorism and natural or man-made disasters.” May is in Estonia for an EU meeting.

subject: politicsNews
title: Trump says he will announce Paris climate deal decision soon
text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that he will announce “very soon” whether he will pull the United States out of the Paris climate agreement. Answering questions shouted by reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said he was hearing from people on both sides of the issue but would not say whether he had made up his mind. “I'm hearing from a lot of people, both ways. Both ways,” Trump said.

subject: worldnews
title: Catalan government weighing snap election, pro-independence CUP says
text: MADRID (Reuters) - The Catalan government is considering calling a snap election, CUP politician Carles Riera of the pro-independence party said on Tuesday, adding that the far-left party would oppose such a move. “The regional elections are a weapon to cancel the Oct. 1 (referendum) and the will of the majority of Catalonia,” Riera told a news conference. Secessionists in Catalonia say the banned Oct. 1 independence vote, which drew only 43 percent turnout and was largely shunned by Catalans who want to stay in Spain, gives them a mandate to claim statehood.

subject: worldnews
title: Japan's Abe says North Korea policy must be changed through stronger pressure
text: TOKYO (Reuters) - Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe said on Tuesday that it is important to change North Korea's policy by applying greater pressure than ever before. Abe told reporters that Japan wants to lead efforts to alter Pyongyang's course through close cooperation with the international community. On Monday the United Nations Security Council unanimously tightened sanctions on North Korea over its sixth and most powerful nuclear test on Sept. 3, banning textile exports and capping crude oil imports.

subject: worldnews
title: Car bomb kills seven in Mogadishu, police say
text: MOGADISHU (Reuters) - A car bomb exploded near a bus stop in a district of Somalia's capital Mogadishu on Thursday, killing seven people, police said. It was not immediately clear who was responsible. The Islamist group al Shabaab has frequently bombed Mogadishu and other towns as it tries to destabilize the western-backed central government. “I have counted seven dead bodies of civilians,” police officer Major Nur Hussein told Reuters by phone, adding that the car blew up just as a minibus carrying civilians was passing and that the death toll was likely to rise. A Reuters witness at the scene said he saw at least three dead bodies and a damaged, bloodstained minibus.

subject: worldnews
title: Iraqi Kurdish opposition party Gorran urges Barzani to resign
text: BAGHDAD (Reuters) - Gorran, a leading opposition party to Iraqi Kurdish leader Masoud Barzani, called on Sunday for his resignation and for the formation of a “national salvation government” to handle the crisis between the Kurds and Iraq's central authorities. Gorran, also known as the Change Movement, blamed Barzani for the “disaster” facing the Kurds after they lost the oil-rich city of Kirkuk on Oct. 16 to Iraqi forces, who seized it in response to a Kurdish independence referendum held last month despite warnings from Baghdad, Iran and Turkey. “The Kurdistan presidency must be dissolved and a national salvation government be formed to overcome the current situation,” the party leadership said in a statement issued after meeting in the Kurdish city of Sulaimaniya. Gorran supports Iraqi Kurds' right to self-determination but opposed holding the Sept. 25 referendum, saying the timing was ill-chosen.

subject: worldnews
title: Merkel open to the idea of a European finance minister
text: BERLIN (Reuters) - German Chancellor Angela Merkel said on Friday that she could well imagine a European finance minister, but stressed that such a post would have to be backed by substantive reforms. “We certainly need to strengthen the governance of the euro zone ... I have nothing against a European finance minister. I can well imagine that,” she told a joint news conference in Berlin with French Prime Minister Edouard Philippe. “But what is important to me is that we underpin the slogans - ‘economic government' and ‘European finance minister' and ‘budget' - with substance.” Merkel added that while monetary policy in the euro zone is harmonized, economic cooperation remains “incoherent.”

subject: worldnews
title: Minister: PM May showed 'guts and grace' in conference speech
text: LONDON (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Theresa May showed guts and grace by pressing on with her keynote speech to the Conservative Party conference despite a repeated coughing fit and an interruption by a prankster, business minister Greg Clark told Sky on Thursday. “She showed guts and grace,” Clark told Sky News, adding that there was enormous warmth toward May in the conference hall. May's attempt to reassert her waning authority was undermined on Wednesday when her speech was disrupted by repeated coughing, a prankster, and even letters from her slogan falling off the set behind her.

subject: worldnews
title: Belgian police detain four over foiled 2015 attack on high-speed train
text: BRUSSELS (Reuters) - Belgian police have detained four people in connection with the foiled August 2015 attack on a high-speed train linking Brussels and Paris, federal prosecutors said on Monday. In that attack, a gunman armed with a machine gun wounded three people on the train before passengers overpowered him; it was one in a series of militant attacks to hit Belgium and France over the past two years. Police carried out six house searches in Brussels and elsewhere in Belgium early on Monday but found no explosives or weapons. Prosecutors said a judge will decide later whether the detainees will be held further.

subject: worldnews
title: New Zealand's kingmaker party to announce government decision Thursday
text: WELLINGTON (Reuters) - New Zealand's small nationalist party, New Zealand First, said in a statement on Wednesday that it would be ready on Thursday afternoon to announce the formation of the next government. The party holds the balance of power after the inconclusive Sept. 23 election, in which neither the ruling National Party nor the opposition Labour Party won enough seats to form a government on its own.

subject: worldnews
title: Bulgaria asks Russia's MiG to overhaul its fighter jets
text: SOFIA (Reuters) - Bulgaria has asked Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG to overhaul and maintain its 15 aging MiG-29 fighter jets under a four-year contract worth up to 81.3 million levs ($49 million), the defense ministry said on Monday. NATO and EU member Bulgaria must keep its Soviet-era aircraft flying after plans to buy eight new fighter jets hit another snag. The ministry will essentially have to restart the process and has yet to send requests for proposals to aircraft makers. The main contenders remain Sweden's Saab with its Gripen jets, Portugal and the United States with used F-16s, and Italy with used Eurofighter Typhoons. Defence Minister Krasimir Karakachanov has said Bulgaria could also send a request to Boeing for F-18 aircraft. ($1 = 1.6586 leva)

subject: worldnews
title: U.S. air strike causes casualties during Mattis visit to Kabul
text: KABUL (Reuters) - A U.S. air strike called in to repel an attack in Kabul on Wednesday, while Defense Secretary Jim Mattis was visiting the Afghan capital, caused a number of civilian casualties, the NATO-led Resolute Support mission said. The strike was called in to support an Afghan Special Forces unit fighting attackers who targeted Kabul airport, but a missile malfunctioned, “causing several casualties,” the statement said. The two leaders also agreed that the recent U.N. subject: politicsNews

text: LONDON (Reuters) - Presumptive Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump said that Britain leaving the European Union would make no difference to a potential bilateral trade deal if he were elected, according to an interview clip aired by ITV on Sunday.
